dataGovernanceStatus.role: Represents governance/epistemic credibility of the record.
dataGovernanceStatus.behavior: IMMUTABLE. For authoritative gazetted geometries, status is OFFICIAL at birth and remains OFFICIAL perpetually. An official 2016 baseline never becomes un-official.

temporalSupersessionLifecycle.role: Represents temporal active/superseded status in the spatial timeline.
temporalSupersessionLifecycle.behavior: valid_to closes open-ended boundaries (NULL -> DATE >= valid_from). is_current transitions from true -> false upon supersession (for historical baseline, strictly false at birth).

fieldLifecycleRules.forbiddenTransitions: Any mutation of status triggers SQLSTATE 23514.

fieldLifecycleRules.permittedTransitions: true -> false (active geometry retired upon adoption of superseding boundary order).
fieldLifecycleRules.forbiddenTransitions: false -> true prohibited for historical statutory baselines.

NULL -> closed DATE >= valid_from (when open-ended boundary is superseded).
fieldLifecycleRules.forbiddenTransitions: Altering an already-closed valid_to date; setting valid_to < valid_from.

fieldLifecycleRules.permittedTransitions: Automatically set to now() on permitted valid_to or is_current updates.

sourceFidCollisionHandling.architecturalAnalysis: Within the generic entity_geometries schema, mandal_version_id has a UNIQUE index (uq_entity_geometries_mandal_version). A table-wide unique constraint on (dataset_version_id, source_feature_id) is deliberately avoided to prevent imposing cadastral FID uniqueness assumptions on future non-cadastral or multi-part datasets.
sourceFidCollisionHandling.enforcementMechanism: The W016 Ingestion Contract enforces source-FID collision prevention transactionally and fail-closed: inside the ingestion transaction, an explicit assertion query verifies that no existing record with the same dataset_version_id and source_feature_id is mapped to a different mandal_version_id. If any collision is detected, the transaction immediately fails closed with SQLSTATE 23514.
